Here is a concise, ready-to-use 12-week plan summary that integrates the running progressions, tempo work, explicit intervals, strength work, and asthma-friendly safety notes. It’s structured for a 3-run-per-week model (Sessions A, B, C) plus two optional strength days (S1, S2) each week. Week 13 finisher/race-day prep has been noted as a follow-up option, but the core 12 weeks are below.

Overview
- Goals: Build: aerobic base, running economy, and confidence; introduce interval and tempo work; reach a comfortable 5K distance with sustainable pace; incorporate asthma-safe warm-ups, airflow strategies, and recovery.
- Weekly structure: 3 running sessions (A: shorter intervals; B: longer intervals; C: tempo/easy + mobility), 2 optional strength days (S1, S2), daily mobility. 2–3 strength movements per session, 8–12 reps, 2–3 sets; core work included.
- Key asthma management: pre-exercise SABA as prescribed, 8–12 minute dynamic warm-up, warmer air strategies in cold weather, monitor symptoms, adjust intensity, carry inhaler, stay hydrated.

Weekly layout (Sessions A, B, C) with strength days S1, S2
- Session A: Interval-focused with shorter work bouts
- Session B: Interval-focused with longer work bouts
- Session C: Tempo or easy run with mobility; optional light run
- S1 and S2: Full-body strength workouts, 2 days per week, alternating weeks

Week-by-week plan (12 weeks)
Week 1
- A: 5-min warm-up; 1 min jog / 2 min walk × 6; total running ~6 min
- B: 5-min warm-up; 90 sec jog / 2 min walk × 6; total running ~9 min
- C: Mobility plus easy 15-min walk
- S1: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps of goblet/bodyweight squats, push-ups or incline push-ups, dumbbell rows or inverted rows, glute bridges, step-ups; plus 2–3 core moves
- S2: Optional light version of Week 1 S1 exercises or a separate mobility/activation session

Week 2
- A: 2 min jog / 2 min walk × 5
- B: 1.5 min jog / 2 min walk × 6
- C: Mobility + light conditioning; tempo: 5-minute tempo jog (optional) after warm-up
- S1/S2: Same structure; slightly progress sets/reps if comfortable

Week 3
- A: 3 min jog / 2 min walk × 4
- B: 2 min jog / 1.5 min walk × 6
- C: Mobility + easy run; tempo segment (e.g., 6 minutes) within run if feeling good
- S1/S2: Continue progression

Week 4
- A: 4 min jog / 2 min walk × 4
- B: 3 min jog / 2 min walk × 5
- C: Cross-training option 20–25 min; tempo block if tolerable (6–8 minutes)
- S1/S2: Strength focus with steady load

Week 5
- A: 5 min jog / 2 min walk × 3
- B: 4 min jog / 1.5 min walk × 4
- C: Mobility + light run; tempo blocks totaling ~8–9 minutes split
- S1/S2: Maintain 2–3 sets; consider slight load increase if form is solid

Week 6
- A: 6–7 min jog / 2 min walk × 2
- B: 5 min jog / 2 min walk × 3
- C: Mobility + conditioning; tempo ~10 minutes total across run
- S1/S2: Increase reps or load modestly if tolerated

Week 7
- A: 8–9 min jog / 2 min walk × 2
- B: 6–7 min jog / 2 min walk × 2
- C: Tempo day continues; tempo blocks ~12 minutes total
- S1/S2: Maintain strength with emphasis on control and posture

Week 8
- A: 9–11 min jog / 1.5–2 min walk × 2
- B: 7–8 min jog / 2 min walk × 2
- C: Mobility + optional easy run; tempo blocks totaling ~12–14 minutes
- S1/S2: Keep two days; reduce volume slightly if Parkrun test is planned that week

Week 9
- A: Build toward longer continuous blocks; target 14–18 minutes total running across session
- B: 10–12 min jog blocks × 2 cycles with 1–2 min walk as needed
- C: Easy conditioning + mobility; light tempo if symptom-free
- S1/S2: Maintain two days

Week 10
- A: 16–20 minutes continuous running total
- B: 12–14 min jog blocks × 2 cycles with 30–60s walking recoveries
- C: Strength maintenance; optional light run
- S1/S2: Maintain; keep intensity moderate

Week 11
- A: 22–24 minutes continuous running (minimal walking breaks)
- B: 14–16 min jog blocks × 2 cycles
- C: Mobility + gentle cross-training
- S1/S2: Maintain

Week 12
- A: 25–28 minutes continuous easy run or 3–4 min run / 1–2 min walk pattern totaling 25–30 minutes
- B: 15–20 minutes easy run focusing on form and rhythm
- C: Taper recovery + mobility; optional light tempo if energy allows
- S1/S2: Lightening the load and volume to allow recovery

Tempo/Interval pacing cues
- Tempo day: aim for a steady, controlled “comfortably hard” pace (roughly 7–8/10 effort); breathing controlled; can nasal-breathe during warm-up, mouth-breathe during tempo
- Interval days (A): work intervals start easy and progress; targets per week should stay below symptom threshold
- Interval days (B): longer intervals; pace closer to tempo or controlled race-pace for the given week
- Recovery: easy jog or brisk walk between intervals

Strength progression (S1 and S2)
- Weeks 1–4: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps; focus on form and activation
- Weeks 5–8: Increase load or reps to 12 per set where comfortable; consider short tempo finishes
- Weeks 9–12: Maintain two sessions/week with lighter loads if tapering; emphasize mobility, core, glute activation, and posture

Strength examples (quick reference)
- S1: Goblet squat, walking lunges, hip hinge (Romanian deadlift or single-leg), glute bridges, push-ups, dumbbell rows, Pallof press or suitcase carry, dead bug
- S2: Step-ups, Bulgarian split squat, hip hinge variation, hamstring curls or glute/ham progression, shoulder press, band pull-aparts or prone YTW, side planks

Asthma safety notes
- SABA as prescribed, quick access inhaler
- Warm-up and cool-down emphasize slow airway conditioning
- Cold weather: indoor runs when possible; cover mouth with scarf or mask
- If symptoms arise: reduce pace or volume; switch to walking; use inhaler per plan; resume when symptoms subside
- Hydration and breathing: hydration strategy around training; diaphragmatic breathing practice during cool-down

Optional Week 13 finisher / race-day prep
- If you want, Week 13 can be added as a tapering/finisher week that focuses on race-day strategies, a final light race-day simulation, and mental rehearsal.

Here’s a 12-week couch-to-5K plan tailored for a 24-year-old with exercise-induced asthma (on a SABA inhaler). It emphasizes a progressive mix of walking, running, mobility, and conditioning, with careful warm-up/cool-down routines, airway management considerations, and recovery. It’s designed for 3 sessions per week, with optional extra conditioning days if motivation and symptoms allow. Adjust as needed based on how he feels and any medical advice.

Key considerations
- Pre-exercise: use SABA inhaler as prescribed 5–15 minutes before workouts if he’s instructed to do so by his physician.
- Warm-up: dynamic mobility and gradual-intensity cardio for 8–12 minutes, ending with a short, low-intensity run if tolerable.
- Cold air management: in winter or cold environments, consider indoor intervals (treadmill) or wearing a scarf/face mask to warm air; adjust intensity if bronchospasm signs appear.
- Asthma symptoms: if coughing, wheezing, chest tightness, or shortness of breath beyond mild effort, reduce intensity or stop and use rescue inhaler as directed, then resume only when symptoms resolve.
- Recovery: emphasize sleep, hydration, and nutrition supportive of training; consider a daily mobility/soft-tissue work routine on rest days.
- Progression: weekly incremental increases in running time while maintaining brisk walking portions to keep gradual exposure and reduce airway stress.

Program overview
- Weeks 1–4: establish base aerobic endurance with walk/run intervals, focus on technique and consistency.
- Weeks 5–8: increase running blocks, introduce longer continuous runs with walk breaks, begin basic conditioning work.
- Weeks 9–12: transition to more continuous running, reach near-5K target distance with a gradual taper to race pace for the final week.

Weekly structure (3 workouts per week)
- Session A: Run/walk interval workout
- Session B: Run/walk interval with increased running time
- Session C: Easy conditioning + mobility + optional light run

Week-by-week plan

Week 1
- Session A: 5-minute brisk walk warm-up; intervals: 1 minute jog / 2 minutes walk × 6 cycles (total running ~6 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes walking; light stretching.
- Session B: 5-minute brisk walk; intervals: 90 seconds jog / 2 minutes walk × 6 cycles (total running ~9 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility and core plus a 15-minute walk at comfortable pace.

Week 2
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 2 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 5 cycles (total running ~10 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 1.5 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 6 cycles (total running ~9 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility, light strength (bodyweight squats, glute bridges, planks 20–30s), 15–20 minute easy walk.

Week 3
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 3 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 4 cycles (total running ~12 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 2 minutes jog / 1.5 minutes walk × 6 cycles (total running ~12 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility + core work; 15–20 minute easy outdoor walk or treadmill.

Week 4
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 4 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 4 cycles (total running ~16 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 3 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 5 cycles (total running ~15 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Easy cross-training option (cycling, elliptical) 20–25 minutes at comfortable pace; mobility.

Week 5
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 5 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 3 cycles (total running ~15 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 4 minutes jog / 1.5 minutes walk × 4 cycles (total running ~14 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Strength and mobility circuit (2 rounds: bodyweight squats 12, push-ups or incline push-ups 8–12, single-leg deadlifts 8 per side, glute bridges 15, Bird-Dog 10 per side) plus 15 minutes easy walk.

Week 6
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 6 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~12 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 5 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 3 cycles (total running ~15 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility plus light conditioning: 15–20 minutes cycling or brisk walk; core circuit (planks 30–40s, side planks 20–30s each side, dead bug 10 reps per side).

Week 7
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 8 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~16 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 6 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~16 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Strength-focused with lighter loads; 3 rounds: goblet squats or dumbbell squats 12, push-ups 10, DB rows 12 per arm, Romanian deadlift 12.

Week 8
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 9 minutes jog / 1.5 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~18 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 7 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~18 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility + optional 20–25 minute easy run if symptom-free; otherwise maintain walk/run intervals.

Week 9
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; continuous run build: 2 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 6 cycles → shift gradually: 5 minutes jog, 3 minutes walk? Use a plan: 10 minutes jog total broken by 2-minute walk. Aim for longer running blocks; total running ~20 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 10 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~20 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Easy conditioning: cycling or swimming 20–30 minutes, plus mobility.

Week 10
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 12 minutes jog / 2 minutes walk × 1 cycle → aim to do 18–20 minutes of running total with short walks as needed. Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 8 minutes jog / 1.5 minutes walk × 2 cycles (total running ~16 minutes). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Strength maintenance; 3 rounds: lunges 10 per leg, push-ups 10–15, inverted row or TRX row 12, hip thrust 12; 20 minutes overall.

Week 11
- Session A: 5-minute warm-up; continuous run progression: 22–24 minutes total running with minimal walking breaks; if needed, use 1–2 minutes walk breaks spread out.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; intervals: 12 minutes jog / 1 minute walk × 2 cycles (total ~24 minutes running). Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session C: Mobility + gentle cross-training 20–25 minutes; optional light jog.

Week 12
- Session A: Race-pace prep: 5-minute warm-up; 5K readiness: 25–28 minutes of continuous easy running if symptom-free, or run 3–4 minutes with 1–2 minutes walk as needed, aiming to accumulate 25–30 minutes of running total. Cool-down 5 minutes.
- Session B: 5-minute warm-up; easy run 15–20 minutes, focusing on pace and form; optional strides: 4 × 20 m at controlled faster pace to practice form.
- Session C: Taper recovery: mobility work, light core, 15–20 minutes easy walk or cycle; reinforce breathing strategy and stretching.

Race week (simulated 5K goal)
- If he’s feeling good and symptoms are controlled, plan a goal: 5K event or test run on the weekend after a gradual taper (reduce volume by ~20–30% from Week 11, keep intensity light to moderate).
- Ensure warm-up includes 10 minutes of dynamic mobility and a 5–10 minute light jog, followed by a few short strides.

Strength/conditioning guidelines (2 days per week, optional)
- Focus on full-body movements with emphasis on breathing mechanics and posture.
- Example: 2 sets per exercise, 8–12 reps, moderate load:
  - Goblet squats
  - Dumbbell or bodyweight rows
  - Romanian deadlifts or hip hinge hinges
  - Step-ups
  - Push-ups or incline push-ups
  - Planks and side planks
- Core work: 2–3 sets of 20–40 seconds planks, dead bug, bird-dog.

Mobility and recovery
- Daily 5–10 minutes of mobility: ankle, hip openers, thoracic spine rotation, chest/shoulder mobility.
- Post-workout: 5–10 minutes of gentle stretching focusing on calves, hip flexors, hamstrings, glutes, chest, and shoulders.
- Sleep: aim for 7–9 hours per night; hydration: 2–3 liters per day depending on body weight and climate.
- Breathing drills: diaphragmatic breathing practice during cool-down; nasal breathing during warm-up when possible to promote airway conditioning.

Nutrition considerations
- Balanced meals with protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day for recovery and muscle synthesis (adjust to body weight).
- Carbohydrates around workouts to fuel runs (1–3 g/kg in the hours before exercise depending on tolerance and timing).
- Hydration strategy around sessions; consider electrolyte prior to long sessions if sweating heavily.
- Post-workout recovery: within 30–60 minutes, consume a mix of carbs and protein (e.g., yogurt and fruit, smoothie with protein, or a balanced snack).

Safety and adjustments
- If cold air triggers symptoms, use a scarf or mask over mouth/nose, consider indoor treadmill workouts during colder days.
- If ever symptoms persist after inhaler use or worsen, stop exercising and follow asthma management plan; consult physician if needed.
- Monitor progress: keep a training log with distance, pace, perceived exertion, and any asthma symptoms to tailor progression.

Rationale
- The plan gradually increases running time in a controlled manner, with walk breaks to reduce airway stress and sustain exercise confidence.
- Warm-ups and cool-downs are emphasized to minimize bronchospasm risk and improve recovery.
- Optional strength and mobility work supports running economy, reduces injury risk, and helps sustainable progress toward a 5K.

Tempo/Interval pacing cues
- Tempo day: aim for a steady, controlled “comfortably hard” pace (roughly 7–8/10 effort); breathing controlled; can nasal-breathe during warm-up, mouth-breathe during tempo
- Interval days (A): work intervals start easy and progress; targets per week should stay below symptom threshold
- Interval days (B): longer intervals; pace closer to tempo or controlled race-pace for the given week
- Recovery: easy jog or brisk walk between intervals

Strength progression (S1 and S2)
- Weeks 1–4: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps; focus on form and activation
- Weeks 5–8: Increase load or reps to 12 per set where comfortable; consider short tempo finishes
- Weeks 9–12: Maintain two sessions/week with lighter loads if tapering; emphasize mobility, core, glute activation, and posture

Strength examples (quick reference)
- S1: Goblet squat, walking lunges, hip hinge (Romanian deadlift or single-leg), glute bridges, push-ups, dumbbell rows, Pallof press or suitcase carry, dead bug
- S2: Step-ups, Bulgarian split squat, hip hinge variation, hamstring curls or glute/ham progression, shoulder press, band pull-aparts or prone YTW, side planks

Asthma safety notes
- SABA as prescribed, quick access inhaler
- Warm-up and cool-down emphasize slow airway conditioning
- Cold weather: indoor runs when possible; cover mouth with scarf or mask
- If symptoms arise: reduce pace or volume; switch to walking; use inhaler per plan; resume when symptoms subside
- Hydration and breathing: hydration strategy around training; diaphragmatic breathing practice during cool-down
